clue.text: Unnerve character returning in rickety old car

parts.note: to unnerve someone is to rattle them

indicators.note: returning tells us to read the word for character from back to front

parts.note: a character in a play is a part or role

explanation.surface: A nervous driver is shaken up, in character, as their battered old banger comes home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unnerve' looks like the definition, but the car is at the end; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattletrap is an informal name for a decrepit, noisy vehicle that shakes as it goes.

clue.text: Actual region's miles off

indicators.note: off tells us the letter for miles is removed from the region word

parts.note: a realm is a region or domain; the 's is just 'is' joining to the next words

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the real distance to a region is miles out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes M from REALM.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that genuinely exists rather than being imagined.

clue.text: Restaurant pastry dish knocked over — a riot breaks out

indicators.note: in a down clue, knocking something over turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a tart is a dish made of pastry with a filling

indicators.note: a riot that breaks out scatters, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In a restaurant, a pastry dish is sent flying as a riot erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns TART into TRAT; 'breaks out' rearranges A RIOT into TORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian eating house, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Drunk started smoking

definitions.meaning: slang for intoxicated, as after many drinks
to light a cigarette and begin puffing on it

explanation.surface: Someone drunk who also took up cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for tipsy and also literally means having lit a cigarette or pipe.

clue.text: Take care of fencing trouble — back part only

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the care word surrounds the trouble word

parts.note: to tend something is to look after it
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Look after a fence that's giving trouble, but only the part at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' is not the sport but enclosing; 'only' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear or final section of something is its last portion, as of a queue or a procession.

clue.text: Clothes variously appear on line

indicators.note: variously suggests the letters appearing in different arrangements

explanation.surface: Clothes are shown in different ways on the washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variously' rearranges APPEAR into APPARE; 'on' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for garments or dress.

clue.text: Ruin in Madrid is here

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tourist reports that the ruin they want to see is here in Madrid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters at the end of Madrid and start of 'is here'. 'Ruin' looks like a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to dish someone's hopes is to wreck or spoil them.

clue.text: I doze before end of broadcast — that's not appropriate

parts.note: a nap is a short doze

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A listener admits nodding off before a programme finishes, which is rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives the last letter of broadcast; 'before' and 'that's' link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or ill-fitting, the opposite of apt.

clue.text: Unpredictable schoolgirl supporting it in writing

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes after
in tells us the word it goes inside the writing word

parts.note: your hand is your handwriting
taken as written
a miss is a young girl, as in the form of address

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl's handwriting backs up her essay, but its quality is erratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing' stands for the hand you write in; in a down answer 'supporting' means placed underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hit-and-miss is erratic, sometimes succeeding and sometimes failing.

clue.text: What a golfer may get on tee to one side?

parts.note: a golfer may score a par, the expected strokes for a hole
tee is the sound of the letter T

explanation.surface: A golfer standing on the tee wonders what score is possible, while shanking the ball sideways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means separately or aside, at some distance from others.

clue.text: Leading man drinking wine in it

indicators.note: in puts the combined piece inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the man word swallows the wine

parts.note: taken as written
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: The star actor is in it, glass of wine in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading man' reads as a phrase, but 'Leading' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading and important both describe someone of high rank or significance.

clue.text: Most of army unit's recommended diet

indicators.note: most of tells us to drop the final letter of the army word

parts.note: a regiment is a unit of the army; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Most soldiers in the unit follow the recommended diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet, exercise or treatment.

clue.text: One progresses rapidly in this designer outfit?

definitions.meaning: the highest ratio in a car's gearbox, used for speed
fashionable clothes from the best labels

explanation.surface: A smart designer outfit lets you move ahead fast.
explanation.walkthrough: TOP GEAR is also a long-running British TV motoring programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the highest gear of a vehicle and, read loosely, top-quality clothing.

clue.text: Hit it off, being mature

definitions.meaning: to get along well with someone
getting on means growing old, advancing in years

explanation.surface: Two people became friends once they were grown up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to have a friendly relationship and also, as 'getting on', to be ageing.

clue.text: Carol happy to change? That's questionable

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Is Carol happy to change? That's doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges CAROL HAPPY; 'That's' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocryphal story is of doubtful authenticity, widely told but probably untrue.

clue.text: Very thirsty chap — red ordered

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters being put into a different order

explanation.surface: A man desperate for a drink orders red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges CHAP and RED together.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched literally means dried out, so figuratively extremely dry in the throat.

clue.text: Hornblower and his capital short speech

indicators.note: capital means the first letter, as a capital letter starts a word
short tells us to cut off the last letter of the speech word

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A naval hero gives a brief address in his capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' gives H from his; 'short' trims ORATION to ORATIO. Horatio Hornblower is C. S. Forester's fictional Royal Navy officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional naval captain created by C. S. Forester bears this first name.

clue.text: Awkward type wrestling endlessly for one-time payment?

parts.note: a lump is a clumsy, ungainly person

indicators.note: endlessly tells us to remove the final letter of the wrestling word

parts.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling

explanation.surface: A clumsy fellow takes up wrestling and is paid off once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts SUMO to SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump sum is a single payment made at one time rather than in instalments.

clue.text: Small fruit with perfect flavour

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pear is a fruit
mint condition means perfect, unused

explanation.surface: A little fruit with an ideal taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a type of mint widely used to flavour chewing gum and sweets.

clue.text: Annoyance shown by King George during succession

indicators.note: during means within, so the king goes inside the succession word

parts.note: a chain is a succession or series of linked things
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, as on postboxes

explanation.surface: A historian notes irritation shown by King George during the royal succession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or mortification at having failed or been humiliated.

clue.text: Famous London prison — deny wife being incarcerated

indicators.note: being incarcerated means locked inside, so the wife letter goes inside the deny word

parts.note: to negate is to deny or nullify
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies

explanation.surface: A man denies his wife is locked up in a notorious jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was the City of London's main prison for centuries until 1902.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate Prison stood near the Old Bailey and was notorious for its harsh conditions.

clue.text: Come clean about one written about female saints

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: written about means wrapped round, so the word one encloses the female letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone owns up about a letter written concerning women saints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' puts F inside ONE to make ONFE.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is an idiom for admitting the truth, owning up to wrongdoing.

clue.text: Girl, 22, in frolics

indicators.note: frolics suggests letters playing about and changing places

parts.note: the number refers to the solution of 22 across, a vessel

explanation.surface: A girl is having fun on the boat from another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolics' rearranges the 22 answer together with IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cynthia is a girl's name, an epithet of the moon goddess Artemis.

clue.text: Vessel in Scottish river coming back with companion on board

indicators.note: on board means inside, so the companion letters go within the reversed river
coming back tells us the river's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A boat heads back down a Scottish river with a friend aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed river gives YAT before the companion goes aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or motor vessel used for pleasure or racing.

clue.text: Jazz band — old doctor in company

indicators.note: in tells us the old doctor pieces sit inside the company letters

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A jazz group features an elderly physician among its members.
explanation.walkthrough: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a common crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small group of musicians, especially playing jazz or dance music.

clue.text: Exotic brew in a bistro, perhaps

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange or foreign, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual drink is served in a little restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic' rearranges BREW IN A; 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is one example of a small place serving drinks, here a place for wine.

clue.text: Severely criticise book ending a series

parts.note: the last one is the final item in a series

explanation.surface: A critic slates the final book of a series.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast a person or thing is to attack them strongly in words.

clue.text: Game is extremely pricey

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extremely picks the letters at the extremes of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A shopper complains a board game costs far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives P and Y, the ends of pricey.
explanation.definitionFit: I-spy is a children's guessing game based on objects seen around you.

clue.text: Therapist's in work, at hospital

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
op is short for opus, a work
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A therapist is at work at the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here but means at home; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A homeopath practises an alternative system of treatment using tiny doses of substances.

clue.text: Sign in accounts — no comment

indicators.note: no means without, so the word comment is taken out

parts.note: commentaries are accounts or descriptions of events
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spokesperson declines to say anything about the signature in the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes COMMENT from COMMENTARIES; 'in' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Spoils play

definitions.meaning: plunder or booty taken in war or theft
Joe Orton's 1965 black comedy of that title

explanation.definitionFit: The word means stolen goods and is also the title of Joe Orton's farce.

clue.text: Rugby ref's award achieved by fine endeavour

parts.note: a penalty is a fine or punishment
to try is to make an endeavour or attempt

explanation.surface: A rugby referee rewards a team for a well-made effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'achieved by' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the referee grants this score when foul play stops a probable try.
